Meta's FY2025 MD&A projects an escalating capital commitment to AI, disclosing $69.69 billion of purchases of property and equipment in 2025 and anticipating capital expenditures of approximately $115 billion to $135 billion in 2026 to support AI efforts and the core business [1]. Research and development expenses in 2025 increased $13.50 billion, or 31%, compared to 2024, driven mostly by higher employee compensation and infrastructure costs related to AI initiatives, while the company's investment philosophy explicitly frames generative AI and superintelligence as requiring "significantly increased investment in infrastructure [2][3]."

Against that spending posture, the risk factors caution that "there can be no assurance that the usage of AI will enhance our products or services or be beneficial to our business, including our efficiency or profitability," and that "AI may not develop in accordance with our expectations" while "market acceptance of features, products, or services we build is uncertain [4][5]." The risk factors further state that Meta's "AI strategy and investments may not be successful in the foreseeable future, or at all," and that the company regularly makes significant changes to product roadmaps as its understanding of the technological challenges of AI continues to evolve [5]. The risk factors also note that the company continues to incur substantial costs and "may not be successful in generating profits" from its AI efforts [6].

A specific monetization tension involves Reels: the MD&A acknowledges that Reels is growing in usage but monetizes at a lower rate than Feed and Stories products and is expected to continue to monetize at a lower rate for the foreseeable future, while AI-driven investment is simultaneously being directed toward promoting Reels [3][7]. The risk factors reinforce this by noting that the company may introduce new features or changes that attract users away from properties where it has more proven means of monetization, citing Reels as an example, and warning these decisions may adversely affect business results and may not produce the long-term benefits expected [7]. The MD&A also acknowledges that legislative, regulatory and platform developments are expected to continue to adversely impact advertising revenue for the foreseeable future, even as AI-driven improvements to ad targeting and measurement are described as long-term initiatives [8].

The deepest structural tension is that the MD&A acknowledges the ability to support AI investments is dependent on generating sufficient profits from other areas of the business, while simultaneously disclosing that Reality Labs reduced the company's 2025 overall operating profit by approximately $19.19 billion and that 2026 Reality Labs operating losses are expected to remain similar to 2025 [3][9]. The risk factors sharpen this by stating that "some of these investments, particularly our significant investments in Reality Labs, have generated only limited revenue and reduced our operating margin and profitability, and we expect the adverse financial impact of such investments to continue for the foreseeable future," directly linking the AI and RL investment programs to the risk that the profits needed to fund them may themselves be under pressure [9][10]. Free cash flow in 2025 was $43,585 million, compared to $52,103 million in 2024, as the surge in property and equipment purchases offset the increase in operating cash flows, illustrating how the scale of infrastructure investment is already constraining the residual cash available even before the larger 2026 program begins [11].
